shortDescription: CSX NASDAQ:CSX generated record revenue in the third quarter as higher fuel surcharges, higher volumes, and increased shipping charges across merchandise, intermodal, and coal resulted in a 12% increase to $4.02B, $60M better than Wall Street anticipated.Across merchandise segments, nearly all (exc…

children: as higher fuel surcharges, higher volumes, and increased shipping charges across merchandise, intermodal, and coal resulted in a 12% increase to $4.02B, $60M better than Wall Street anticipated.
Across merchandise segments, nearly all (except fertilizers) realized increased sales from a year ago, although only chemicals beat Wall Street’s estimates. Combined, CSX
saw an 11% increase in merchandise shipping revenue to $2.45B versus $2.43B estimates.
Intermodal revenue increased 20% to $634M (vs. $651.5M), while coal increased 10% to $537M vs. $528.3M estimates. Trucking revenue increased by 10% to $227M, which was $2M more than expected.
shipped 1.69M units, an increase of 5% from the same quarter last year, while intermodal volume was up 7%.
Operating margin expanded 880 basis points to 39.1%, beating estimates by 170 basis points better than expected.

earned a profit of $0.57 per share, up 54% year-over-year and three cents above estimates. This accounts for $170M more in fuel costs to $451M, $53M in incentive compensation, and $38M more in wage and healthcare cost inflation, all of which were partially offset by a $164M decrease in goodwill impairment expenses.
The results drove shares more than 4% higher in after-hours trading. Peers Union Pacific
will report third quarter results on Thursday.

title: Intermodal and coal help drive CSX to record Q3 revenue
